Name: Chicago Basketball Scoreboard Desk Display
Short description: The Chicago Basketball Scoreboard is a small always-on desk display that follows your teams over Wi-Fi: record, standings, next game, and the live score when they play. Ships ready to set up with a 3D-printed stand.
Description:
The Chicago Basketball Scoreboard puts your team's season on your desk. For Chicago basketball fans. Eighty-two games is a lot to keep track of. Sports Meter shows where your team stands, when they play next, and the live score with the quarter and clock when they do. Pictured in Chicago's red and black; you choose the team at setup and can change it any time.

What your Chicago Basketball Scoreboard shows

  • Live score with the quarter and clock
  • Season record, winning or losing streak, home and away splits
  • Place in the conference or division
  • Next game in your local time, with the channel
  • GAME DAY: the next-game card lights up in your team's colors
  • Men's and women's, pro and college

The screen takes on your team's colors, and shows its logo once it is connected.

Pictured following the Chicago Bulls. Pick any team at setup; the screen takes on that team's colors and logo.

Not just basketball: add up to six teams from any mix of football, basketball, baseball, hockey and soccer, and they take turns on screen.

This Chicago Basketball Scoreboard works for teams in the NBA, the WNBA and college basketball (men's and women's).

Setting up your Chicago Basketball Scoreboard

Setup takes about a minute: scan the code on the screen, choose your Wi-Fi and your teams. Change teams any time from your phone without setting up Wi-Fi again. No app, no account, no subscription.

In the box: Sports Meter display, 3D-printed desk stand, USB-C cable, quick-start card.

Good to know: Needs 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi. Scores usually trail the live action by well under a minute. Updates itself over Wi-Fi.

Sports Meter is an independent product made by Encinitas 3D. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, sponsored by or licensed by any league, team, conference or broadcaster. League and team names are used only to describe the scores and schedules the device can display, and remain the property of their owners.
